title: Ch 13 Test: Our Environment
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.

questions.q: Which group contains only biodegradable items?
options: Fruit peels, cake and lime juice
questions.answer: (b) Fruit peels, cake and lime juice

questions.q: Which of the following forms a food chain?
Which of the following are environment-friendly practices?
options: Switching off unnecessary lights and fans
Walking to school instead of being dropped by scooter

questions.q: In a food chain, the energy passed on to the next trophic level is about:
options: the same as the previous level
questions.answer: (a) 10% of the previous level (10 per cent law)

questions.q: Depletion of the ozone layer is mainly caused by:
**Assertion (A):** Food chains generally have only three or four trophic levels.  **Reason (R):** The energy available decreases greatly at each successive trophic level.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (a). After a few levels, too little energy is left to support another level.

questions.q: What are decomposers? What would happen if there were no decomposers?
questions.answer: Decomposers are micro-organisms, such as bacteria and fungi, that break down the dead remains and waste products of organisms into simpler substances. Without them, dead bodies and wastes would pile up, and nutrients would not be returned to the soil for plants to use.

or.q: How is ozone formed in the upper atmosphere? Write the equations.
or.answer: High-energy ultraviolet (UV) radiation splits oxygen molecules into free oxygen atoms: O_{2} → O + O. Each free oxygen atom combines with an oxygen molecule to form ozone: O + O_{2} → O_{3}.

questions.q: What is biological magnification? Why is it highest in organisms at the top of a food chain?
questions.answer: The progressive build-up of non-biodegradable chemicals, such as pesticides, at each trophic level of a food chain. Organisms at the top eat many organisms from the levels below, and these chemicals are not broken down, so the concentration keeps increasing up the chain.

questions.q: Study the food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle

subparts.q: Identify the producer and the tertiary consumer.
If 10,000 J of energy is available at the producer level, how much energy will reach the snake?
Which organism will have the highest concentration of a pesticide that enters this food chain? Why?
subparts.answer: The eagle. It is at the top of the food chain, and pesticides build up at each level (biological magnification).

questions.q: Why is damage to the ozone layer a cause for concern? What steps have been taken to limit it?
questions.answer: The ozone layer shields the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun. UV radiation can cause skin cancer and harm other living things. Ozone levels fell sharply in the 1980s because of CFCs, which are used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers. In 1987, UNEP succeeded in forging an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels, and companies now make CFC-free refrigerators.

or.q: Suggest three ways in which you can reduce the waste your household produces.
or.answer: (Any three) Separate biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste. Compost kitchen waste. Carry cloth bags instead of plastic bags. Avoid single-use plastic items. Reuse containers. Send paper, glass and metal for recycling.

subparts.q: What is an ecosystem? Name its two types of components, with examples.
subparts.answer: An ecosystem is made up of all the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living parts of their environment. Biotic components are living things such as plants, animals and micro-organisms. Abiotic components are physical factors such as temperature, rainfall, wind, soil and minerals.

subparts.q: Explain the flow of energy in an ecosystem. Why is it unidirectional?
subparts.answer: Green plants capture about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves and convert it into food energy. This energy passes from producers to herbivores to carnivores, but only about 10% is passed on to each next level. The rest is used for life processes or lost as heat. Energy that passes to the next level never comes back to the previous level, so the flow is in one direction only.

or.q:
(a) Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances, with two examples of each. [2]
(b) Give three ways in which non-biodegradable substances harm the environment. [3]
or.answer: (a) Biodegradable substances are broken down by bacteria and other decomposers (e.g. vegetable peels, paper, wood, cotton). Non-biodegradable substances are not broken down by biological processes (e.g. plastic, polythene, glass, DDT). (b) Any three: they stay in the environment for a long time; they pollute the soil and water; pesticides enter food chains and build up (biological magnification); plastic blocks drains and harms animals that swallow it.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Some years ago, it was proposed that tea on trains should be served in disposable kulhads (clay cups) instead of plastic cups. It was soon realised that making kulhads on such a large scale would cause the loss of fertile top soil. Now, disposable paper cups are commonly used.

subparts.q: Why was it proposed to replace plastic cups?
subparts.answer: Plastic is non-biodegradable and pollutes the environment.

subparts.q: What was the problem with using kulhads on a large scale?
Give one advantage of paper cups over plastic cups and one over kulhads.
subparts.answer: Over plastic: paper is biodegradable (and can be recycled). Over kulhads: making paper cups does not use up fertile top soil.
